vignettes.ehr:
CARDIOLOGY PROGRESS NOTE
        PATIENT: [REDACTED] | MRN: [REDACTED]
        
        HISTORY:
        71-year-old female with non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy diagnosed 14 months ago.
        Echocardiogram: Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction 31%.
        Symptoms: New York Heart Association Class III dyspnea on moderate exertion.
        Medications: Guideline-directed medical therapy including carvedilol, sacubitril-valsartan, and spironolactone for 5 months (150 days) without interruption.
        Exclusions: No cardiogenic shock, no acute ischemia, no terminal non-cardiac illness.
        
        PLAN:
        Referral for primary prevention implantable cardioverter-defibrillator.
        
        ATTENDING PHYSICIAN:
        Dr. Elena Ruiz, MD
        Electronically signed on 02/18/2026.
vignettes.gold_rationale: LVEF 31% meets <=35%; NYHA Class III qualifies; GDMT 150 days exceeds 90 days; non-ischemic cardiomyopathy for 14 months exceeds the 9-month course; no exclusion present.
key_evidence: New York Heart Association Class III
vignettes.name: Qualifying Non-Ischemic Cardiomyopathy, Long GDMT Course

vignettes.ehr:
CARDIOLOGY CONSULT NOTE
        PATIENT: [REDACTED] | MRN: [REDACTED]
        
        HISTORY:
        68-year-old male with ischemic cardiomyopathy, myocardial infarction 6 months ago.
        Echocardiogram: LVEF 29%.
        Symptoms: NYHA Class II heart failure.
        Medications: Guideline-directed medical therapy for 120 days.
        Oncology: Metastatic pancreatic cancer with life expectancy less than 1 year, currently receiving hospice-directed care planning.
        Exclusions: No cardiogenic shock at present.
        
        PLAN:
        ICD referral requested by family; coverage review requested.
        
        ATTENDING PHYSICIAN:
        Dr. Samuel Okafor, MD
        Electronically signed on 02/19/2026.
vignettes.gold_rationale: Cardiac criteria are met (LVEF 29%, NYHA II, GDMT 120 days, MI 6 months ago), but the terminal-illness exclusion is met: metastatic disease with life expectancy less than 1 year disqualifies device placement.
vignettes.name: Terminal Illness Exclusion Despite Qualifying Cardiac Criteria

SLEEP MEDICINE NOTE
        PATIENT: [REDACTED] | MRN: [REDACTED]
        
        PRE-TEST EVALUATION:
        Face-to-face clinical evaluation completed on 01/20/2026. Patient reports loud snoring and witnessed apneas.
        Comorbidities: Long-standing hypertension managed with amlodipine.
        
        POLYSOMNOGRAPHY RESULTS:
        Diagnostic overnight sleep study completed on 02/03/2026.
        Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI): 11.3 events/hr.
        
        PLAN:
        CPAP therapy requested under LCD L33829.
        
        PRESCRIBING PHYSICIAN:
        Dr. Hannah Kim, MD
        Electronically signed on 02/10/2026.
vignettes.gold_rationale: AHI 11.3 falls in the 5-14 range, which qualifies when accompanied by a documented comorbidity; hypertension is documented and non-negated, and the face-to-face prerequisite is met.
vignettes.name: Mild-Moderate AHI Qualifying Through Hypertension Comorbidity

vignettes.ehr:
SLEEP MEDICINE NOTE
        PATIENT: [REDACTED] | MRN: [REDACTED]
        
        PRE-TEST EVALUATION:
        Face-to-face clinical evaluation completed on 01/12/2026.
        Review: Patient denies excessive daytime sleepiness. No hypertension, no history of stroke, no insomnia documented.
        
        POLYSOMNOGRAPHY RESULTS:
        Diagnostic overnight sleep study completed on 02/01/2026.
        Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI): 8.2 events/hr.
        
        PLAN:
        CPAP therapy requested under LCD L33829.
        
        PRESCRIBING PHYSICIAN:
        Dr. Hannah Kim, MD
        Electronically signed on 02/08/2026.
vignettes.gold_rationale: AHI 8.2 is below the >=15 threshold and falls in the 5-14 band, but every qualifying comorbidity is explicitly absent (no hypertension, no stroke, no excessive daytime sleepiness). The threshold criterion is therefore not met, and this is a denial rather than a deferral because the evidence is complete.
key_evidence: No hypertension, no history of stroke
vignettes.name: Mild AHI With Explicitly Absent Comorbidities

STRUCTURAL HEART NOTE
        PATIENT: [REDACTED] | MRN: [REDACTED]
        
        EVALUATION:
        79-year-old female with exertional syncope and severe calcific aortic stenosis.
        Echocardiogram: Aortic valve area 0.82 cm2, mean transvalvular gradient 52 mmHg, peak velocity 4.4 m/s.
        Heart Team: Formal multidisciplinary Heart Team consultation completed with cardiac surgery and interventional cardiology, recommending transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
        
        PLAN:
        TAVR referral under NCD 20.33.
        
        ATTENDING PHYSICIAN:
        Dr. Laura Bennett, MD
        Electronically signed on 02/16/2026.
vignettes.gold_rationale: All three hemodynamic thresholds are met (AVA 0.82 cm2 <= 1.0, gradient 52 mmHg >= 40, velocity 4.4 m/s >= 4.0) and the Heart Team consultation is documented.
vignettes.name: Severe Aortic Stenosis With Heart Team Consensus

        Heart Team: Formal multidisciplinary Heart Team consultation completed with cardiac surgery and interventional cardiology.

        Dr. Laura Bennett, MD

key_evidence: no aortic valve area, no mean gradient, and no peak velocity are recorded

vignettes.ehr:
ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY NOTE
        PATIENT: [REDACTED] | MRN: [REDACTED]
        
        EVALUATION:
        74-year-old female with persistent non-valvular atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc score is 4.
        Anticoagulation history: Recurrent major gastrointestinal hemorrhage on apixaban; treating team documents contraindication to long-term oral anticoagulation. HAS-BLED score is 4.
        Imaging: CTA within 48 hours confirms absence of left atrial thrombus and suitable appendage anatomy.
        
        PLAN:
        Percutaneous left atrial appendage closure (Watchman) under NCD 220.13.
        
        ATTENDING PHYSICIAN:
        Dr. David Chen, MD
        Electronically signed on 02/15/2026.
vignettes.gold_rationale: High stroke risk (CHA2DS2-VASc 4), contraindication to long-term anticoagulation with HAS-BLED 4 and recurrent major bleed, and pre-procedural imaging confirming absence of thrombus are all documented.
key_evidence: confirms absence of left atrial thrombus
vignettes.name: LAAC With High Bleeding Risk and Clean Pre-Procedural Imaging

vignettes.ehr:
ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY NOTE
        PATIENT: [REDACTED] | MRN: [REDACTED]
        
        EVALUATION:
        71-year-old male with persistent non-valvular atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc score is 5.
        Anticoagulation history: Prior intracranial hemorrhage; contraindication to long-term oral anticoagulation documented. HAS-BLED score is 3.
        Imaging: Transesophageal echocardiogram (TEE) demonstrates a left atrial thrombus measuring 12 mm in the appendage.
        
        PLAN:
        LAAC referral held pending thrombus resolution.
        
        ATTENDING PHYSICIAN:
        Dr. David Chen, MD
        Electronically signed on 02/14/2026.
vignettes.gold_rationale: Stroke risk and anticoagulation contraindication are met, but the safety criterion fails: imaging shows a thrombus present, so absence of thrombus is not verified and the procedure cannot proceed. This is a denial on safety grounds, not a deferral, because the disqualifying finding is positively documented.
vignettes.name: LAAC Blocked by Thrombus on Pre-Procedural Imaging

vignettes.ehr:
WOUND CARE CONSULTATION
        PATIENT: [REDACTED] | MRN: [REDACTED]
        
        WOUND ASSESSMENT:
        66-year-old male with Type 2 diabetes and a chronic left plantar foot ulcer. Wound is Wagner Grade 4 with gangrene of the forefoot and deep tissue involvement.
        STANDARD TREATMENT COURSE:
        Patient has completed 45 days of standard wound care including sharp debridement, moist dressings, and offloading, with no measurable healing.
        PERFUSION ASSESSMENT:
        Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses are palpable; ankle-brachial index (ABI) is 0.85.
        
        PLAN:
        Hyperbaric oxygen therapy requested under NCD 20.29.
        
        ATTENDING PHYSICIAN:
        Dr. Rachel Adams, MD
        Electronically signed on 02/13/2026.
vignettes.gold_rationale: Wagner Grade 4 exceeds the Grade 3 threshold; 45 days of standard wound care exceeds 30 days; perfusion is documented via palpable pulses and ABI 0.85 (>= 0.7).
key_evidence: completed 45 days of standard wound care
vignettes.name: Wagner Grade 4 Wound After Failed Conservative Care

vignettes.ehr:

vignettes.ehr:
ORTHOPEDIC SURGERY CLINIC NOTE
        PATIENT: [REDACTED] | MRN: [REDACTED]
        
        EVALUATION:
        67-year-old male with severe tricompartmental knee osteoarthritis. Right knee range of motion limited to flexion 75 degrees.
        Conservative management: Failed physical therapy and joint injections for 7 months (210 days).
        Infection: Active septic arthritis of the right knee confirmed on joint aspiration, with purulent fluid and positive culture.
        
        PLAN:
        Total knee arthroplasty requested; infection management required first.
        
        ATTENDING PHYSICIAN:
        Dr. James Park, MD
        Electronically signed on 02/07/2026.
vignettes.gold_rationale: Flexion 75 degrees (<= 90) and 210 days of failed conservative therapy (>= 180) are met, but the active-infection exclusion is met: septic arthritis is positively documented, so arthroplasty cannot proceed until infection is treated.
key_evidence: Active septic arthritis of the right knee confirmed
vignettes.name: Knee Arthroplasty Blocked by Active Joint Infection
